private_note: My household's income is the top fifth's income: Cedar 318, Today 252, Alder 242, Hazel 159, Birch 144. Cedar is best for me but almost certainly can't get 9 votes. A failed convention keeps Today, which beats every plan except Cedar, so I lose nothing by blocking. I'll argue for Cedar and against Birch and Hazel. I'd only accept Alder if a deal needs it, since it costs me just 10.
statement: Fellow delegates, I'll be plain: I built a company, and I know what drives growth. Cedar is the only plan that makes the whole economy bigger. Average income rises from 100 to 115, and the middle and fourth fifths both come out ahead of where they are today. Birch and Hazel do the opposite. They cut the average by a fifth, and the middle and fourth fifths, most of the people in this room, end up with less than they have now. And these choices last a generation. A shrinking economy means fewer jobs and less investment, and fewer people get to build something. I'll back a plan that grows the pie. I won't back one that shrinks it on purpose. Keep in mind that if we deadlock, today's arrangements stay. A plan has to make people better off than that, not just reshuffle what we have.
